title: Global proteomics insights for a novel small compound targeting the non-integrin Laminin Receptor in a macrophage cell model.
authors: Haffner, Abigail; Neto, Manoel Figueiredo; Umbaugh, C Samuel; Sobreira, Tiago J P; Lescun, Timothy B; Sintim, Herman O; Figueiredo, Marxa L
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子化合物靶向非整合素层粘连蛋白受体（LR）的抗炎作用，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白界面对接与蛋白组学网络，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Monocytes and macrophages are the first barrier of the innate immune system, which interact with agents causing osteoarthritis or other conditions, leading to the release of proinflammatory mediators that exacerbate inflammation. METHODS: The aim of this study was to investigate the proteomic changes in THP-1 monocytes differentiated to macrophages, pre- or -post small compound treatments and in the presence or absence of a proinflammatory stimulus, Lipopolysaccharide (LPS). This study aimed to discover and isolate small compounds that mimic the interaction between Pigment derived growth factor (PEDF) and its 37/67 kDa Laminin receptor (LR) with potential anti-inflammatory activity. RESULTS: Our results suggested that novel compounds targeting the LR-PEDF interface can be useful for modulating anti-inflammatory effects. Several compounds were selected based on in silico docking at the PEDF/LR interface and examined for their ability to reduce IL-1beta expression in a macrophage cell model. Compound C3 showed the highest efficacy in reducing IL-1beta expression in the presence of LPS proinflammatory stimulus. Proteomics analysis revealed that C3 treatment altered the global proteomic profile of THP-1 activated macrophages, affecting pathways such as MYC targets, oxidative phosphorylation, and mTORC1 signaling. DISCUSSION: The analysis also highlighted the involvement of key regulators, including RPSA and MYC, and their interactions with other proteins such as ribosome proteins and cell cycle regulators. Furthermore, the downregulated proteome analysis revealed shared and unique pathways affected by the treatments, including processes related to actin cytoskeleton, translation, and the inflammatory response. Protein-protein interaction networks suggested the potential involvement of transcription factors like MYC and the interconnectedness of signaling pathways in mediating such as the effects of the treatments. Overall, these findings provide valuable insights into the potential anti-inflammatory activity and underlying mechanisms of compound C3, emphasizing its relevance for further investigation in the context of inflammatory conditions.
abstract_zh: 引言：单核细胞和巨噬细胞是先天免疫系统的第一道屏障，它们与导致骨关节炎或其他疾病的因子相互作用，引发促炎介质释放，从而加剧炎症。方法：本研究旨在探讨THP-1单核细胞分化为巨噬细胞后，在有无小分子化合物处理及有无促炎刺激物脂多糖（LPS）存在下的蛋白质组学变化。本研究旨在发现并分离模拟色素上皮衍生因子（PEDF）与其37/67 kDa层粘连蛋白受体（LR）相互作用且具有潜在抗炎活性的小分子化合物。结果：我们的结果表明，靶向LR-PEDF界面的新型化合物可用于调节抗炎效应。基于PEDF/LR界面的计算机模拟对接筛选出若干化合物，并检测其在巨噬细胞模型中降低IL-1β表达的能力。化合物C3在LPS促炎刺激存在下降低IL-1β表达的效果最为显著。蛋白质组学分析显示，C3处理改变了THP-1活化巨噬细胞的整体蛋白质组谱，影响MYC靶点、氧化磷酸化和mTORC1信号传导等通路。讨论：分析还强调了关键调控因子（包括RPSA和MYC）及其与其他蛋白质（如核糖体蛋白和细胞周期调控因子）相互作用的参与。此外，下调蛋白质组分析揭示了处理所影响的共享和独特通路，包括与肌动蛋白细胞骨架、翻译和炎症反应相关的过程。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络提示转录因子如MYC的潜在参与以及信号通路在介导处理效应中的相互关联性。总体而言，这些发现为化合物C3的潜在抗炎活性及其潜在机制提供了宝贵见解，强调其在炎症性疾病背景下进一步研究的相关性。
